Research prototype report · generated 2026-10-16 from saved results by scripts/build_report.py · git cd44f69 (local branch claude/blissful-faraday-2unozw, not pushed) · status: research prototype, not publication-ready · no novelty claim is made.

1. Executive summary (plain English)

What we set out to test. Whether a new kind of neural network building block, the Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN), helps a “functional autoencoder” predict time-to-event from patient-like or machine-like measurements that change over time, compared with a matched conventional network (an MLP).

What we did.

  • Built the prototype in small validated stages:
    • a survival-likelihood module that correctly handles incomplete (censored) follow-up;
    • a simulator with a known answer;
    • the functional representation and our own KAN layer;
    • the models;
    • evaluation metrics.
  • Checked each stage against independent reference calculations before moving on.

The most important result.

  • Before comparing KAN with MLP, we required the conventional functional autoencoder to pass a pre-agreed learnability check: on simulated data with a known answer, it had to get close to the best achievable accuracy. It did not.
    • Required: a concordance (C-index) of at least 0.8636.
    • Achieved: 0.8361, even after the two permitted repairs (longer training, more capacity).
  • The likely reason is that the risk depended on the size of an oscillation, and the model’s first layer can only take weighted averages of the curves, which cannot directly measure size when the oscillation’s timing varies.
  • Under the rule we fixed in advance, this blocked the KAN-vs-MLP comparison.

So this prototype provides no evidence that KAN helps, and no evidence that it does not. The key comparison was correctly not run.

What did run.

  • Validated, conventional baselines on:
    • simulated data;
    • NASA C-MAPSS turbofan data (real benchmark data with no genuinely incomplete follow-up; mainly a remaining-useful-life benchmark);
    • PBC liver-disease data (real data with genuinely incomplete follow-up).
  • On simulated data, simple per-channel summaries (last value, mean, spread, trend) beat the “weighted-average” FPCA approach. This is consistent with the learnability finding.
  • On PBC, all baselines clearly beat a no-information reference, but they could not be told apart reliably. The PBC patients had only about 3 measurements each before the prediction time, too few for functional modelling to be reliable.

What is still open (your decisions).

  • How to revise the architecture so that it can pass the gate.
  • Which PBC endpoint to adopt.
  • Which C-MAPSS landmark design to adopt.

Test status. 150 test cases; latest outcomes: 148 passed, 1 failed (the learnability check R2), 1 skipped (documented not-applicable case). Every attempt, including failures, is logged.

2. Research objective and hypotheses

Narrow research question. Does a KAN-based functional representation improve survival prediction from multivariate time-varying trajectories over parameter-matched conventional baselines?

Hypotheses were fixed in docs/design.md §8.3 and docs/experiment_protocol.md §6 before any experiment ran (decision D24):

ID Status Hypothesis Outcome in this prototype
H1 (primary) pre-registered On synthetic setting P0, the KAN functional autoencoder + AFT has lower survival-curve error than the parameter-matched functional MLP autoencoder + AFT (paired over 5 replicates). Not tested. Blocked by the failed learnability gate (§10.1, D33).
H2 (secondary) pre-registered A reconstruction term (α > 0) reduces survival-curve error vs survival-only training (α = 0). Not tested (blocked, D33).
H3 (secondary) pre-registered Functional encoders outperform the flattened autoencoder under sparse sampling. Not tested (blocked, D33).
Gate R1–R3 pre-specified engineering checks The pipeline can learn a known relationship under controlled conditions. R1 PASS, R2 FAIL, R3 PASS.

The project makes no novelty claim. No literature review was performed (D27).

5. Model architecture, equations and key design choices

The full specification is in docs/design.md.

5.1 Landmark prediction

A trajectory observed on a window ending at landmark s is used to predict the residual time T* − s for individuals at risk at s. No input is dated after s (test K4).

5.2 Censoring-aware AFT likelihood

log T = η + σ ε,    w = (log y − η)/σ,    S(t) = S_ε((log t − η)/σ)
ℓ_i = δ_i [log f_ε(w_i) − log σ − log y_i] + (1 − δ_i) log S_ε(w_i)
Weibull: log f = w − e^w,          log S = −e^w
Log-normal: log f = −w²/2 − ½ log 2π,   log S = log Φ(−w)
Log-logistic: log f = w − 2 softplus(w),  log S = −softplus(w)

5.3 Functional representation

  • Smoother: a quadrature-weighted penalised B-spline smoother (D20): c = (ΦᵀQΦ + λR + λ₀I)⁻¹ ΦᵀQy, with cell-length weights Q. The data term therefore approximates ∫ (y − x)² dt and is consistent under refinement of the sampling (test F3).
  • Functional linear layer: h_j = b_j + Σ_d ∫ β_jd(t) x_d(t) dt = b_j + Σ_d c_dᵀ J b_jd.

5.4 Autoencoders

  • Encoder and decoder: z = g_enc(h); ĉ = g_dec(z); x̂(t) = Σ_k ĉ_k φ_k(t); head η = wᵀ[z, u] + b.
  • Reconstruction loss: weights every individual equally (D19).
  • Total loss: L = mean(−ℓ) + α·L_rec + λ_β Σ bᵀR_βb.

5.5 KAN layer and parameter matching

  • KAN layer (in-house; passed F-KAN-1..4): out_q = Σ_p [w^b_pq SiLU(x_p) + w^s_pq Σ_g a_pqg B_g(x_p)] + bias_q. Cubic B-splines on a uniform grid of 5 intervals on [−2, 2], preceded by a per-feature BatchNorm (D30).
  • Parameter matching (D31): KAN encoder and decoder blocks are chosen automatically to be within ±10% of the MLP blocks, avoiding bottlenecks narrower than r.
    • Original defaults: 2120 vs 2024 parameters (+4.7%).
    • Repaired defaults: 5090 vs 5032 (+1.2%).
    • For D ≥ 6, a decoder hidden width of 3 < r is unavoidable under matching; this is a recorded limitation.

5.6 Key corrections made before any training

  • D30: BatchNorm instead of LayerNorm. A per-sample LayerNorm would have removed 2 of the 4 latent degrees of freedom.
  • D31: the matching rule.
  • D32: M2 targets that each model can represent.
  • D36 (later): linear-AFT penalty scaling, found during the C-MAPSS smoke test.

6. Datasets, sources, dimensions, missingness and preprocessing

Dataset Kind Source / provenance Dimensions used Outcome
Synthetic SYNTHETIC src/kanfae/data/synthetic.py; replicate seeds 1000–1004; gate seed 21 N = 1000 per replicate, D = 3 channels, 8–40 points per channel (dense) or 3–8 (sparse) Weibull or log-normal AFT with known η; independent censoring 0 / 30 / 60%
C-MAPSS FD001 REAL (simulated turbofan) PHM Society mirror of the NASA Prognostics Data Repository; SHA-256 in run_manifest.json; Saxena & Goebel (2008) 100 training engines (life 128–362 cycles, median 199.0); 100 official test engines (length 31–303); 15 informative sensors (constant: s1, s5, s10, s16, s18, s19, os3) Run to failure; no censoring; RUL benchmark
PBC sequential REAL (right-censored) CRAN survival 3.8-12, object pbcseq; SHA-256 in run_manifest.json 312 patients, 1945 visits; landmark cohort 278 at 730 days; 6 lab channels plus age and sex Status 0/1/2 = censored / transplant / dead; E1 and E2 sensitivity analyses

Synthetic data.

  • Observed and oracle objects are separate (tests G5, G6, M5).
  • Censoring is independent of everything, so marginal-KM IPCW is appropriate by construction (D17).
  • 15% of each test individual’s points (for individuals with ≥ 4 points) are held out for reconstruction metrics.

C-MAPSS.

  • Inspected before any loader was written (reports/logs/cmapss_inspection.json). There are no missing values and cycles are consecutive.
  • Note: the dataset readme lists the columns up to “sensor measurement 26”, but there are 26 columns and 21 sensors.
  • Sensors are selected on training engines only (standard deviation ≥ 1e-6).
  • Option A uses the full history [1, s0] with s0 = minimum training-split life − 1.
  • Option B uses trailing 30-cycle windows every 10 cycles, with s/100 as a covariate. Engine-level splits (K3) and no input after the landmark (K4) are tested.

PBC.

  • Help page vs data:
    • the follow-up column is futime (the help page says time);
    • trig and copper are listed but absent;
    • chol is 42% missing and was excluded (D26);
    • missing visit rows: alk.phos 3.1%, platelet 3.8%.
  • Channels: log(bili), albumin, log(alk.phos), log(ast), platelet, log(protime). Missing values are masked (never imputed into the loss).
  • The help page documents that extra visits were often prompted by worsening condition.

Explanations (each failure got at most two targeted repairs; no threshold was changed, D11).

  • Stage A, A2 (all three families), attempts 1–2: test-harness bugs.
    • Quadrature over (−∞, ∞) overflowed exp(u) and gave NaN.
    • A wide finite range then missed the narrow density peak at σ = 0.2.
    • Repair 2 integrates on the standardised scale w.
    • The likelihood code itself was never changed.
  • Stage A, A7 (log-logistic, then log-normal): the reference optimiser.
    • Our maximised log-likelihood was 7.8e-4 higher than lifelines’.
    • lifelines’ SLSQP stopped early.
    • A diagnostic showed our likelihood evaluated at lifelines’ own estimates equals lifelines’ value within 1e-8.
    • Tightening lifelines’ ftol resolved it.
  • Stage E, Q1, attempts 1–2: fixture issues.
    • The scikit-survival reference cannot evaluate the training censoring KM beyond the largest training time.
    • Our IBS now evaluates G at min(Y_i, t_last), which is exact.
    • The fixture uses test times inside the support.
  • Stage D, learnability gate: R2 FAILED after both permitted repairs (§10.1).

9. Baselines, splits, seeds, tuning rules and metrics

Models actually run (validated, non-neural).

Model Representation Head
FPCA + AFT FPCA scores Linear Weibull AFT
FPCA + Cox FPCA scores (secondary reference) Cox
Summary + AFT Last value, mean, sd, OLS slope per channel, plus u Penalised linear Weibull AFT
Summary + Cox Same summary features Penalised Cox
Summary + RSF Same summary features Random survival forest, 200 trees
  • References (not comparators, no tuning): a covariate-free Kaplan–Meier prediction (km_null, D35) and, on synthetic data only, the true model (oracle_true).
  • Not run (BLOCKED, D33): functional MLP autoencoder, KAN functional autoencoder, flattened autoencoder, and all ablations AB1–AB8.

Splits.

  • Synthetic: 5 independent replicate data sets (seeds 1000–1004), each split 60/20/20, stratified on δ.
  • C-MAPSS: 5 engine-level splits (seeds 0–4). Official test engines are evaluated separately.
  • PBC: 5 patient-level splits, stratified on δ.

Leakage controls. Fitted on training data only (test K2):

  • channel standardisation;
  • smoother λ;
  • FPCA;
  • sensor selection;
  • summary-feature scaling;
  • the censoring models;
  • all hyperparameters.

Tuning (D22).

  • Each model gets 4 configurations at seed 0, selected by validation IBS.
  • Grids:
    • FPCA: r ∈ {2, 4, 8, 12}
    • Summary AFT: L2 ∈ {1e-3, 1e-2, 0.1, 1} (per observation)
    • Summary Cox: penaliser ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10}
    • RSF: min_samples_leaf ∈ {5, 10, 20, 40}
  • The selected RSF configuration is re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and averaged within the replicate. Deterministic models run once.

Metrics (protocol §5, D6).

  • Synthetic primary: survival-curve error, mean_i (1/t_max) ∫₀^{t_max} |Ŝ_i − S_i| dt.
  • Real data primary: IBS with marginal-KM IPCW. For PBC this is flagged as a limitation (D17), with a conditional (Cox censoring model) IPCW sensitivity analysis.
  • Secondary: Uno’s C (truncated at the 90th percentile of test times); Harrell’s C; D-calibration (10 bins); calibration-in-the-large at the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile horizons.
  • C-MAPSS RUL: RMSE and MAE of the median predicted residual life (uncapped), reported separately from survival metrics.

Uncertainty. Mean ± SD over replicates or splits. The pre-registered paired test was planned for H1 only, and H1 was not run. Comparisons between baselines are descriptive.

10. Experimental results

All results below are actual outputs of logged runs (reports/experiment_results.jsonl and .csv; summaries in reports/tables/). Values are mean ± SD over 5 replicates or splits. For the random survival forest, values are first averaged over seeds 0–2 within each replicate. n is the number of replicates/splits contributing.

Data labels. §10.2 is SYNTHETIC. §10.3 is REAL (C-MAPSS, simulated turbofan; RUL benchmark, no natural censoring); its survival-framing metrics involve no censoring, except in §10.3.3, which is ARTIFICIAL CENSORING. §10.4 is REAL (PBC, genuinely right-censored).

10.1 Learnability gate (SYNTHETIC; seed 21; N = 2000; stage D)

  • R1 PASS. An MLP AFT head given the true latent parameters (a, b, A, ω) reached test C = 0.8910 (oracle 0.8936), with σ = 0.4816 (truth 0.5). The survival head and likelihood can learn the known nonlinear relationship when the right features are available.

  • R2 FAIL (pre-specified: C ≥ oracle − 0.03 = 0.8636, and mean probe R² ≥ 0.8). For the functional MLP autoencoder:

    Attempt Change Test C Probe R² (a, b, A, ω) Mean probe R²
    1 As specified 0.7545 0.861 0.711 0. 0.022 0.398
    2 Repair 1: training budget 400 → 3000 epochs (the cap was always hit) 0.8050 0.8 0.525 0.257 0.035 0.404
    3 Repair 2: capacity, H 16 → 32, hidden 32 → 64 0.8361 0.799 0.468 0.449 0.166 0.471

  • R3 PASS at attempt 3.

    • |C − C_R2| = 0.0042.
    • The censoring-aware model had a smaller survival-curve error than the naive model (censored times treated as events) at all 3 seeds: aware 0.0958, 0.0976, 0.0998 vs naive 0.1472, 0.1451, 0.1487.
    • At attempts 1 and 2, the |C − C_R2| part failed (0.0313, 0.0247) while the censoring part already passed.

Diagnosis (interpretation, labelled as such).

  • The largest risk term is −0.8·A², where A is the amplitude of a sinusoid with a random phase. That is a phase-invariant (quadratic) functional of the trajectory.
  • The architecture’s first layer computes only linear functionals ∫β(t) x(t) dt. The downstream network must learn the energy-like combination, and at N = 1200 training individuals it under-fits: train C ≈ test C ≈ 0.79–0.84 in reports/logs/diag_R2_capacity.log. Capacity beyond H = 32 did not help (plateau ≈ 0.836).
  • Consequence (pre-registered rule, D33): the KAN-vs-MLP primary comparison (H1), H2, H3 and all ablations were not run.
  • Diagnostic observation only, not evidence for H1: in one gate-data run at a single seed with a 3000-epoch budget, the KAN autoencoder reached C = 0.837 vs 0.805 for the MLP at its original size (reports/logs/diag_R2_budget.log). This single-seed observation on the gate data set must not be read as a KAN advantage.

10.3 C-MAPSS FD001 (REAL simulated turbofan data; RUL benchmark)

RUL results are reported separately from survival-framing metrics.

  • With no censoring, the IBS here is an unweighted Brier score, and Harrell’s C equals Uno’s C up to truncation.
  • RUL RMSE and MAE use the median of each model’s predicted survival curve, uncapped, in cycles.
  • “Official” means the NASA test trajectories, which have true RUL.
  • Neither landmark option is the approved design (D3b-R). They are separate, labelled analyses.

Observations (descriptive; no significance claims).

  • Option A, internal test. RUL RMSE was 18.4 (FPCA + AFT), 17.9 (FPCA + Cox) and 18.2 (Summary + Cox) cycles, against 47.5 for the null reference.
  • Option A, official test. Only engines whose observed length reaches s0 can be evaluated (mean 54.8 of 100). FPCA + AFT had the lowest RMSE, 23.0.
  • Option B, official test (all 100 engines at their last cycle). Summary + RSF had the lowest RMSE, 18.9. The parametric/Cox baselines were at 27.2–29.4, and the null reference at 44.2.
  • Option B, internal test pooled over all landmarks. RMSE was ≈34.2–37.2. Per band it falls from ≈47.0 at early landmarks (30–99) to ≈10.8 at late landmarks (≥ 200). Discrimination within the early band is modest (C ≈ 0.671), as expected when degradation is not yet visible.
  • The two options are not directly comparable. They predict at different landmarks and evaluate different official-test subsets. This is one reason D3b remains an owner decision.
  • Artificial censoring (Option A).
    • The parametric AFT predictions stayed close to their uncensored values: FPCA + AFT internal RMSE 20.7 vs 18.4.
    • For the Cox models, some predicted survival curves never fell to 0.5 within the training follow-up, so their medians are undefined. On average 1.0 test engines per split were affected for Summary + Cox; these are flagged in the records and set to the grid end. This inflates Cox RMSE (38.6 ± 41.2).
    • For Summary + AFT, all four configurations diverged in one split, so only 4 of 5 splits contribute.
  • The neural autoencoders were not evaluated (BLOCKED, D33).

Endpoint Cohort Events Visits ≤ 730 d: median (range) ≤ 2 visits HR per visit (95% CI) p

Observations (descriptive; no significance claims).

  • All baselines improved substantially on the covariate-free reference for both endpoints.
    • E1: IBS 0.116–0.129 vs 0.204 for the null.
    • E2: IBS 0.133–0.140 vs 0.222.
  • Differences between baselines were small relative to their split-to-split SDs, so no ranking is claimed. With about 56 test patients per split, the uncertainty is large.
  • The conditional-IPCW sensitivity analysis changed IBS values by less than about 0.01.
    • E1: FPCA + Cox 0.116 (marginal) vs 0.114 (conditional).
    • E2: 0.135 vs 0.141.
    • So, under the Cox censoring model used, the metric conclusions are not sensitive to the CA-2 assumption. This does not validate CA-1 for transplant under E1.
  • D-calibration p-values were all > 0.05. With small test sets this test has little power.
  • FPCA-based and summary-feature baselines performed similarly. This is unsurprising given a median of 3 visits per patient (§14). The data are too sparse to make the functional representation informative.
  • Visit process (descriptive). The univariate hazard ratio per additional visit in the window is reported in the table above. The absence of a clear association in this crude check does not rule out an informative visit process; the dataset documentation itself describes visits triggered by worsening condition.

Compute constraints.

  • CPU only (4 cores, no GPU).
  • Neural models were run only for the unit tests, the learnability gate and the gate diagnostics, because the comparisons were blocked.
  • The parameter-matched neural blocks (protocol M3) were verified, but never compared experimentally.

13. What was learned

  1. The censoring-aware AFT machinery is validated. All three AFT likelihoods matched independent references:
    • scipy closed forms (rtol = 1e-10);
    • numerical integration and autograd hazards (1e-8);
    • lifelines maximum likelihood (1e-4);
    • recovery of the truth within 3 SE at a fixed seed.
    The synthetic generator passed all 12 generator criteria, including oracle isolation and invariance of the loss to hidden event times.
  2. The functional representation is numerically sound. Discretisation consistency held at roughly O(1/n²) (F3), and the in-house KAN layer passed its own tests.
  3. The proposed functional autoencoder failed its learnability gate (R2). Under controlled conditions it could not represent a phase-invariant amplitude feature well enough. This is a substantive, negative, architecture-level finding about the linear-functional-first design, and not an implementation bug as far as the diagnostics show. The pre-registered rule therefore prevented any KAN-vs-MLP comparison. The prototype provides no evidence for or against a KAN advantage.
  4. Consistent with point 3, linear-functional baselines (FPCA) were outperformed by simple summary features on synthetic data. Per-channel standard deviation directly carries amplitude information (§10.2). When the risk depended on a non-monotone functional (P-V2), only the nonlinear random survival forest moved clearly away from the null. These are descriptive comparisons, not pre-registered tests.
  5. C-MAPSS and PBC baseline results are descriptive and must be read with the caveats in §14. In particular, C-MAPSS contains no natural censoring, and the two PBC endpoints estimate different quantities.

14. Limitations, possible leakage, censoring assumptions and unresolved decisions

Scope

  • The neural comparisons that motivated the project were not run (D33). All experimental results concern baselines.

Censoring assumptions (D17)

  • The AFT likelihood assumes conditionally independent censoring (CA-1).
  • Marginal-KM IPCW (IBS, Uno’s C) assumes completely independent censoring (CA-2).
  • CA-2 holds by construction for synthetic data and for artificial C-MAPSS censoring.
  • For PBC, CA-2 is doubtful. Under E1, transplant (treated as censoring) plausibly depends on disease severity. The conditional-IPCW IBS is a sensitivity analysis. It replaces CA-2 with CA-1 plus a correctly specified Cox censoring model, so it is not assumption-free.

C-MAPSS

  • No natural censoring. Survival-framing metrics on C-MAPSS are effectively uncensored.
  • Artificial censoring (§10.3.3) tests only the code path.
  • The data are simulated, and failure is defined by the simulator.
  • Option A excludes official test engines shorter than s0.
  • Option B reuses engines across landmarks, so windows are correlated. Splits are engine-level (K3), but pooled metrics mix landmarks; per-band results are also reported.
  • The landmark design decision (D3b) remains unresolved. Both options are reported, and neither is approved as definitive.
  • Integer cycles are treated with the continuous approximation (D25).

PBC

  • Small sample: 278 at risk at 730 days; about 56 test patients per split.
  • Sparse measurements: a median of 3 visits before the landmark (§6). The FPCA representation of such trajectories is weak. Functional modelling of PBC at this landmark should be regarded as unreliable.
  • Informative observation process: documented by the dataset authors (§10.4.3).
  • Endpoint unresolved (D9): E1 and E2 estimate different quantities. Neither is declared definitive. Competing-risks analysis (E3) is not implemented, and no competing-risk claims are made.
  • Baseline covariates: only age and sex. Treatment arm and other baseline variables were not used.

Possible leakage (checked)

  • Splits are by individual or engine (K1, K3).
  • Inputs end at the landmark (K4).
  • Preprocessing, the censoring KM, FPCA and sensor selection are fitted on training data only (K2).
  • Synthetic oracle quantities are isolated (G5, G6, M5).
  • The test-set time grids for IBS and the Uno τ use observed test times. This is standard for evaluation and does not affect fitting.
  • The synthetic t_max comes from the generator’s pilot sample.

Statistical

  • 5 replicates or splits give low precision.
  • Baseline comparisons are descriptive. No multiplicity-adjusted tests were run.
  • STAT tests can fail by chance at their fixed seeds; none failed except R2, which was reproduced deterministically.

Engineering

  • Two bugs were found and fixed during the experiments (D36 penalty scaling, D37 constant Cox columns). All affected results were re-run. Superseded records are kept and labelled.
  • Summary + AFT on C-MAPSS Option A (p ≈ n) often reported converged: false. Its results there are fragile (fit_info).

Literature and status

  • No literature review was performed. The prototype is not publication-ready.

15. Reproducibility

# environment (project-local; never touches the global Python)
bash scripts/setup_env.sh                          # or: KANFAE_FROM_LOCK=1 bash scripts/setup_env.sh
bash scripts/verify_env.sh                         # E-1 / E-5 evidence
# tests (every attempt is appended to reports/logs/test_records.jsonl)
KANFAE_RUN_ID=rerun .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -rA tests/
# data (public sources; checksums in reports/run_manifest.json)
#   C-MAPSS: https://phm-datasets.s3.amazonaws.com/NASA/6.+Turbofan+Engine+Degradation+Simulation+Data+Set.zip
#            -> extract inner CMAPSSData.zip into data/raw/cmapss/
#   PBC:     https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/survival_3.8-12.tar.gz -> data/raw/pbc/{DESCRIPTION,data/pbc.rda}
# experiments (resumable; completed run IDs are skipped)
bash scripts/run_all_experiments.sh                # synthetic (5 replicates x 6 settings) + C-MAPSS (5 splits)
.venv/bin/python scripts/run_cmapss.py --splits 5 --analyses cmapss_A,cmapss_A_artificial --models sum_cox --code-version D37
.venv/bin/python scripts/run_pbc.py --splits 5
# report
.venv/bin/python scripts/compile_test_results.py && .venv/bin/python scripts/aggregate_results.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/make_figures.py && .venv/bin/python scripts/build_report.py
bash scripts/build_pdf.sh && .venv/bin/python scripts/build_manifest.py

Every executed command, with its exit code and timing, is in reports/logs/commands.jsonl. The full outputs are in reports/logs/*.log. The resumable narrative log is reports/logs/execution_log.md.
